title: A monotone density quantity with F -> 1 and lower density omega is at least omega (step 5 of the parent)
statement: Let n be a natural number, alpha, omega, R, Lambda real numbers with alpha > 0, omega > 0, R > 0, and m, F : R -> R. Put Phi(u) := F(u) (m(u)/u^n) + (F(u) - 1). Assume (H1) |F(u) - 1| <= Lambda (u/R)^alpha for every u in (0, R]; (H2) Phi(u) <= Phi(t) whenever 0 < u <= t <= R; (H3) for every epsilon > 0, (1 - epsilon)(omega u^n) <= m(u) for all sufficiently small u > 0 (eventually along the filter u -> 0+). Then omega <= Phi(t) for every t in (0, R].
